Studying the attitude of taxpayers to automation processes. survey was organized among taxpayers to study their opinions regarding the automation of the generation of tax reports. The survey was conducted with about 70,180 respondents (accepted as 100%). About 42.4% of respondents, or 29,744 taxpayers, support tax reporting automation processes, as this significantly reduces the time spent on report preparation. 43.8% of respondents or 30,752 taxpayers responded that this creates great convenience for them, taking into account the elimination of technical errors that arise in the reporting process. And only 13.8% of respondents or 9,684 taxpayers said that, despite the significant time investment, they prefer to prepare the report themselves, since they have enough manpower and time.

The calculation method of the VAT compliance gap was revised following the July mission 2024. This indicator is measuring the "compliance gap." Previously, the PIU was estimating the "total VAT gap" which includes policy and compliance gaps. This explains to a large extent the drastic reduction from the 40% to the 25% threshold.
This coefficient is determined on an annual basis and will be determined based on indicators and data for the year 2024. Reduction in the share of lost VAT for 2023VAT revenues from the Tax Committee - 33,983.5 billion soums. VAT revenues from the Customs system - 43,568.5 billion soums. VAT refund (return) amount from the Tax Committee - 19,666.7 billion soums.
VAT revenues from the Tax and Customs systems minus refunds - 57,885.3 billion soums. Estimated potential volume of VAT revenues â€“ 77,618.8 billion soums Estimated share of lost VAT revenues = (77.6 - 57.9) / 76.6*100 = 25.4%

The calculation method of the VAT compliance gap was revised following the July mission 2024. This indicator is measuring the "compliance gap." Previously, the PIU was estimating the "total VAT gap" which includes policy and compliance gaps. This explains to a large extent the drastic reduction from the 40% to the 25% in 2023.
This coefficient is determined on an annual basis , i.e., the current value is based on the 2024 data.
The coefficient for reducing the share of lost VAT for 2024 VAT revenues from the Tax Committee â€“ 39,567.1 billion soums. VAT revenues from the Customs Committee â€“ 49,029.2 billion soums. VAT revenues from the Tax and Customs Committee â€“ 88,596.3 billion soums. Amount of VAT refunds to taxpayers â€“ 22,803.4 billion soums. Amount of VAT revenues (Tax Code and Customs Code) minus VAT refunds â€“ 65,792.9 billion soums. Estimated potential volume of VAT revenues â€“ 94,672.8 billion soums Share of lost VAT revenues = (94,672.8 â€“ 65,792.9)/94,672.8 = 30.5%

Coefficient for reducing the share of lost VAT for 2023 Receipts from VAT by the Tax Committee - 33,983.5 billion soums. - VAT receipts from the Customs system - 43,568.5 billion soums - Amount of VAT refund (refund) from the Tax Committee - 19,666.7 billion soums - VAT receipts from the Tax and Customs systems less VAT refunds - 57,885.3 billion soum - Estimated potential volume of VAT revenues â€“ 97,716 billion soums Share of lost VAT revenues = (97.7-57.9)/97.7*100= 40.7% Estimated potential volume of VAT revenues was determined based on a micro-simulation financial model presented by IMF experts during the seminars. title.narrative: Coverage of electronic tax services (% total)

comment.narrative: In accordance with the order of the Ministry of Justice dated October 27, 2023 No. 3467, according to the Unified Register of State Services in the Tax Sphere, only 22 types of services provided are included, of which 18 types of services are provided electronically in full, resulting in the level of digitalization of services in the tax sphere in the Public Services system is 72% -. In addition, the Tax Committee is working on the digitization of the general list of tax services. In 2021, the general list of electronic services included 44 types of tax services. In 2022, an additional 7 types of tax services were transferred to electronic form. During the period January-April 2024, an additional 4 types of services were transferred to electronic form, resulting in 55 types of services provided electronically.

title.narrative: Coverage of electronic tax services (% total)

comment.narrative: In accordance with the order of the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Uzbekistan dated October 27, 2023 No. 3467, according to the Unified Register of Public Services in the Tax Sphere, a total of 22 types of services are included. 19 types of services are provided electronically, of which 15 types of services are fully automated, and 4 types of services are mainly electronic, but not fully. 3 types of services have not been transferred to electronic form. To study the need for training and organize training courses based on demand, a survey was conducted in February 2023 among tax authorities remotely through the resource docs.google.com, covering 4,319 employees.

Questionnaires have been prepared to assess the NPS (Net Promoter Score) â€œEmployee Loyalty Indexâ€ for conducting a study among tax authorities (in Uzbek and Russian). The management of the Tax Committee has been notified of a survey among system employees through the Taxes mobile application. By letter of the Tax Committee dated December 29, 2023. 28/2-128972 in the tax system, a study was started through a survey.
During the period January-February 2024 survey was conducted involving 10,308 employees, including 946 managers, 7,191 inspectors and 2,171 support workers. This survey examined the need for professional development among employees.
